# [STORY] As a user, I want movie, user, and actor catalog services with tested REST APIs, so that the platform has real domain data to serve

## User Story
**As a** user
**I want** movie, user, and actor catalog services with tested REST APIs
**So that** the platform has real domain data to serve

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given the movie API, when a client discovers, searches or opens a movie,
      then it gets a TMDB-shaped response, and the second read of that movie is
      served from MongoDB without calling TMDB again
      (`TmdbFacadeIntegrationTest`, #16)
- [x] Given a registered user, when they log in and use profile, favorites or
      watchlist, then user-service serves them from PostgreSQL behind the JWT,
      and rejects the call without one (`UserServiceIntegrationTest`, #17)
- [x] Given the actor API, when a client opens a person, their filmography or a
      search, then actor-service answers from its own PostgreSQL catalog in
      both the TMDB and the native shape (`ActorServiceIntegrationTest`, #18)
- [x] Given the three services, when the stack runs, then each one registers
      with Eureka and serves its OpenAPI document (`OpenApiDocsTest` in all
      three modules, and the newman request "Eureka Registry (core services
      registered)")
- [x] Given the three modules, when the build runs, then line coverage stays at
      or above 80% in each (`./gradlew jacocoTestCoverageVerification`, run by
      `.github/workflows/backend-ci.yml`)

## Definition of Ready
- [x] Meets [Definition of Ready](https://github.com/liviuionesi/lmdb.dev/blob/develop/docs/process/DEFINITION_OF_READY.md)

## Story Points
**Estimate:** 21

## Definition of Done
- [x] Meets [Definition of Done](https://github.com/liviuionesi/lmdb.dev/blob/develop/docs/process/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md)

## Notes
The three services keep separate databases (ADR-002), so favorites and
watchlist store TMDB movie ids only; movie data stays in movie-service.

Audited under #257. The previous body claimed BCrypt strength 10; the code
uses 12.
